b. 
A cattleman and a potential buyer discussed with one another 
sales that had occurred earlier in the day at a local sales barn. 
(The buyer had attended the earlier sales.) The cattleman 
contracted to sell 360 head at $60 a hundredweight to that 
same buyer. Now he knows-as the buyer knew earlier-that 
some cattle had b en sold at the barn for as much as $62 a 
hundredweight. 
Is the contract voidable? See Kanzmeier v. 
McCoppin, 398 N.W.2d 826 (Iowa 1987). 
517 
An individual cannot be held to rely on a statement that is 
obviously false. In a claim based on reliance, a court must 
determine whether or not the falsity of the statement relied 
upon was detectable by ordinary observation. To do so, a 
court takes into account the intelligence and experience of the 
plaintiff and the relationship between the parties involved. In 
this case, those factors lead to a determination that Williams 
knew or should have known that the car did not have air 
conditioning despite the salesman’s statement that it did. 
Williams may not recover for fraud by pleading reliance on 
the salesman’s statement because the statement was 
obviously false.
